MVA Billing Services

Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Follow a Different Playbook Entirely

Billing for a motor vehicle accident case looks nothing like billing a standard insurance claim. Payment usually comes from an auto insurer, sometimes a third-party liability carrier, and often depends on a legal case that hasn't settled yet. A provider can wait months, sometimes years, for reimbursement, and the paperwork trail involves attorneys, adjusters and multiple insurance parties, not just one payer and one patient.

Getting any piece of that wrong, a missed lien filing, an uncoordinated communication between the attorney and the adjuster, a claim aging past a filing deadline, means real money stuck in limbo indefinitely. MVA billing requires a biller who understands both the medical claim and the legal case sitting on top of it.

PMEX manages MVA claims from documentation through settlement, coordinating directly with attorneys and adjusters, tracking liens, and keeping the claim moving so payment doesn't quietly stall behind a case that's still working its way through the legal process.

MVA Billing: Frequently Asked Questions

Standard billing collects from a single insurance payer within weeks. MVA billing involves a legal case, an attorney, an adjuster and often a lien, and payment can take months to resolve depending on when the case settles.

A medical lien secures the provider's right to be paid directly from a future settlement. Filing it correctly and tracking it through the case is essential, since it's often the only guarantee of payment until the case resolves.

Timing depends entirely on how long the underlying legal case takes to resolve, which can range from several months to a few years. PMEX tracks the case status continuously so payment is collected as soon as settlement occurs.

Yes. PMEX coordinates directly with the patient's attorney throughout the case, sharing documentation and lien status through secure channels.

Yes. The PMEX portal gives every party visibility into current case status, so an attorney or adjuster can check progress without needing to call the office.
